plumadraco:study:1.title: Hyperelongate ornamental tail feathers in a new early Cretaceous enantiornithine bird (PLOS One, 2026)

plumadraco:abstract:1.title: Hyperelongate ornamental tail feathers in a new early Cretaceous enantiornithine bird (abstract)

facts.statement: The type locality of Plumadraco is the Jiufotang Formation.
Plumadraco lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian age.
Plumadraco was described by Clark and colleagues.
Plumadraco is known from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) Jiufotang Formation of China.
facts.quote: known from the Early Cretaceous (Aptian age) Jiufotang Formation of China

facts.statement: The genus Plumadraco contains only one species, P. bankoorum, known from a complete skeleton that preserves soft tissues.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Plumadraco bankoorum, known from a complete skeleton preserving soft tissues.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is housed in the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature under accession number STM11-4.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen STM11−4.

facts.statement: The preserved feathers include a pair of elongated tail plumes.
facts.quote: Among the feathers preserved are a pair of elongated tail plumes.

facts.statement: Feathers are preserved around the wings and tail.
facts.quote: Feathers are visible around much of the animal, including the wings and tail.

facts.statement: Plumadraco was a medium-sized enantiornithine bird belonging to the family Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: Plumadraco was a medium‑sized enantiornithine bird belonging to the family Bohaiornithidae.

facts.statement: The estimated body mass of Plumadraco is between 112 and 144 grams.
facts.quote: Its body mass is estimated at 112–144 g

facts.statement: Plumadraco possessed a pair of extremely elongated tail feathers approximately twice the length of its body.
facts.quote: Plumadraco possessed a pair of extremely elongated rectrices (tail feathers), the length of which was approximately twice the body length (excluding the tail)

facts.statement: The tail feathers ended in distinctive rackets at their tips.
facts.quote: The rectrices terminated distally (toward their tips) in distinctive rackets.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the elongated tail feathers were used primarily for display behavior and courtship rituals.
facts.quote: According to Clark and colleagues, such feathers were used primarily for display behaviour and courtship rituals.

facts.statement: The authors suggest the holotype specimen belonged to a male based on the likelihood of sexual dimorphism in similar structures.
facts.quote: Since similar structures are considered a probable indicator of sexual dimorphism in enantiornithines, the authors suggested that the holotype of P. bankoorum belonged to a male.

facts.statement: Plumadraco is classified as a member of Enantiornithes.
Plumadraco is classified in the family Bohaiornithidae.
facts.quote: Plumadraco () is an enantiornithean bird in the family Bohaiornithidae

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Plumadraco as the sister taxon to an unnamed immature bohaiornithid (CUGB-P1202) within a clade that also includes Sulcavis.
facts.quote: They recovered it as the sister taxon to CUGB-P1202, a coeval unnamed immature bohaiornithid, in a clade also including Sulcavis.

facts.statement: It is difficult to determine the specific selection pressures that shaped ornamental feathers in enantiornithines due to limited soft tissue data.
